'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Eastern front of the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Eastern Ukraine offensive]]
****[[Siege of Mariupol]]
*****[[Russian Ground Forces|Russian forces]] resume shelling the port city of [[Mariupol]] after yesterday's [[airstrike]] on a [[children's hospital]] which killed three people. A [[humanitarian aid]] convoy trying to reach the city is also forced to turn back due to heavy fighting. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/world-europe-60685883 (BBC News)]
*[[2022 Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan clashes]]
**An armed incident occurs between border guards at the [[Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border]], killing one Tajik border guard. Following the incident, officials from the [[Batken Region]] in [[Kyrgyzstan]] and the [[Sughd Region]] in [[Tajikistan]] hold talks. [https://en.trend.az/casia/tajikistan/3566586.html (Trend)] [https://www.rferl.org/a/kyrgyzstan-tajikistan-border-shooting/31746784.html (RFE/RL)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Boycott of Russia and Belarus]]
***[[Video game]] companies [[Nintendo]] and [[Sony Interactive Entertainment]] suspend all product sales in Russia. Sony's online [[PlayStation Store]] will also no longer be available in Russia. [https://www.cnbc.com/2022/03/09/sony-suspends-all-playstation-sales-in-russia-over-ukraine-war.html (CNBC)]
***U.S. bank [[Goldman Sachs]] announces that it is closing its operations in Russia, becoming the first major [[Wall Street]] bank to leave the country following the invasion of Ukraine. [https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/goldman-sachs-exit-russia-bloomberg-news-2022-03-10/ (Reuters)]
**[[2022 Russian financial crisis]]
***[[Government of Russia|Kremlin]] spokesman [[Dmitry Peskov]] says that the [[Economy of Russia|Russian economy]] is experiencing a "shock" following an "absolutely unprecedented" [[Economic warfare|economic war]] being waged against the country. Peskov also says that "the economic war that has started against our country has never taken place before. So it is very hard to forecast anything". [https://www.reuters.com/markets/asia/russian-economy-shock-unprecedented-economic-war-kremlin-2022-03-10/ (Reuters)]
***The [[International Monetary Fund]] no longer considers Russian default "improbable", and the [[World Bank]] also considers Russia's and Belarus's default likely. [https://www.reuters.com/markets/europe/imf-chief-georgieva-says-ukraine-war-lower-global-growth-forecast-2022-03-10/ (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/markets/europe/russia-belarus-squarely-default-territory-billions-debt-world-bank-2022-03-09/ (Reuters 2)]
***The [[Central Bank of Russia]] limits withdrawals of [[US dollar]]s, [[euro]]s, [[British pound]]s and [[Japanese yen]] for Russian firms to the equivalent of [[US dollar|$]]5,000, with the withdrawal of larger sums only possible with the Central Bank's permission. The withdrawn funds may only be used for covering overseas work trips. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-central-bank-restricts-firms-access-cash-hard-currency-2022-03-10/ (Reuters)]
**[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] admits that the sanctions have created problems for [[Russia]]. However, he also called the sanctions illegitimate and warned [[Western World|the West]] that Russia will emerge stronger and solve the problems. [https://www.reuters.com/world/putin-says-russia-will-solve-its-problems-calls-sanctions-illegitimate-2022-03-10/ (Reuters)] [https://news.sky.com/story/ukraine-russia-war-latest-news-lavrov-turkey-peace-talks-putin-nuclear-live-updates-12541713 (Sky News)]
**The [[Verkhovna Rada|Ukrainian parliament]] begins to debate a new law which would allow the [[Asset forfeiture|forced seizure]] of all assets belonging to [[Russians]] citizens as well as [[Ukrainians]] deemed by the courts or the [[National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine]] to be Russian collaborators. Last week, a bill was approved that allowed forced seizure of assets owned by the [[Government of Russia|Russian government]] and Russian companies. [https://www.epravda.com.ua/news/2022/03/10/683684/ (''Ekonomichna Pravda'')]
**[[Russia]]'s [[Ministry of Transport (Russia)|Ministry of Transport]] prepares a draft regulation which would allow airlines to not have to honour the request of the lessor to return [[lease]]d aircraft unless a special government commission orders them to do so and would also allow companies to pay the lessor in [[Russian ruble|rubles]]. The law comes amid [[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War|EU sanctions]] which forces all lease contracts for [[Aircraft industry of Russia|Russian aircraft]] to be voided by late March and also forbids E.U. companies from insuring Russian aircraft. [https://www.interfax.ru/russia/827278 (Interfax Russia)]
**[[Russia]] introduces retaliatory sanctions against most foreign countries, with the exception of members of the Russian-led [[Eurasian Economic Union]]. The export of more than 200 items, mostly of technical and agricultural appliances, will also be banned until the end of the year. [https://www.interfax.ru/business/827393 (Interfax Russia)]
**The [[Government of Russia|Russian government]] abolishes penalties for theft of patents if they are held by [[natural person|natural]] or [[legal person]]s from countries considered by the [[Government of Russia|Russian government]] as "unfriendly". The decriminalisation of the [[software piracy|piracy of software]] from "unfriendly" countries is also being considered. [https://www.euractiv.com/section/global-europe/news/russia-legalises-intellectual-property-piracy/ (Euractiv)] [https://www.theregister.com/2022/03/08/russia_software_piracy/ (''The Register'')]
**[[Facebook]] and [[Instagram]] starts to allow users in [[Eastern Europe]], the [[Baltic states|Baltics]], and the [[Caucasus]] to promote violence against Russians and Russian soldiers in the context of the war in Ukraine, which is normally restricted, according to internal emails. A [[Meta Platforms|Meta]] spokesperson states that "As a result of the Russian invasion of Ukraine we have temporarily made allowances for forms of political expression that would normally violate our rules like violent speech such as 'death to the Russian invaders.'" However, calls for violence against Russian [[Prisoner of war|prisoners of war]] and "credible calls for violence against Russian civilians" will remain prohibited. [[Death threat]]s against [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] and [[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] will also be permitted. Meta's spokesperson adds that they are, "for the time being, making a narrow exception for praise of the [[Azov Regiment]] strictly in the context of defending Ukraine, or in their role as part of the [[National Guard of Ukraine|Ukraine National Guard]]," which was previously forbidden. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/exclusive-facebook-instagram-temporarily-allow-calls-violence-against-russians-2022-03-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Around 250 people are evacuated after [[Mount Merapi]] on [[Java]], [[Indonesia]] erupts overnight. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/indonesias-merapi-volcano-unleashes-lava-hundreds-evacuate/2022/03/09/ff2ef490-a00e-11ec-9438-255709b6cddc_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2022 Zagreb Tu-141 crash]]
**A [[Tupolev Tu-141]] [[reconnaissance]] drone crashes on the outskirts of [[Zagreb]], [[Croatia]], triggering a loud blast and forming a large crater, but causing no injuries. The unmanned aircraft flew through [[Hungary|Hungarian]] airspace before crashing in Croatia and is likely to have severely malfunctioned. The aircraft, which travelled 560km, went undetected by both countries' [[air defence]]s. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/mar/11/ukraine-military-drone-crashes-into-croatian-capital-zagreb (''The Guardian'')] [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/flying-object-crashes-croatian-capital-triggers-blast-83383858 (ABC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Niue]]
***[[Niue]] reports its first COVID-19 case since the pandemic began in a person who traveled from [[New Zealand]] and who had tested negative prior to departing. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/mar/10/niue-becomes-second-pacific-island-in-a-week-to-lose-covid-free-status (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
****[[Scotland]] reports a record 14,387 new COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours. [https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/19983691.covid-scotland-14-387-new-cases-41-deaths-recorded/ (''The Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Dakota]]
****[[Governor of North Dakota|Governor]] [[Doug Burgum]] announces that [[North Dakota]] will shift its [[COVID-19]] approach from a [[pandemic]] to an [[Endemic (epidemiology)|endemic]] [[Endemic phase of COVID-19|phase]]. The state health department will also end their COVID-19 updates. [https://apnews.com/article/covid-health-north-dakota-pandemics-4f034647d66f118e51cb36160e30f4ee (AP)] [https://www.kvrr.com/2022/03/10/north-dakota-to-end-daily-covid-19-updates/ (KVRR-TV)]
***[[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****The [[Transportation Security Administration]] and the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] will extend the federal mask mandate [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on public transport|for public transportation]] until April 18. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/03/10/politics/travel-mask-mandate/index.html (CNN)]
***[[History of COVID-19 vaccine development]]
****[[Moderna]] begins a study and a phase 2 trial of a hybrid vaccine aimed at combating the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant|Omicron variant]] with [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|their current]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/moderna-begins-phase-2-trial-for-bivalent-covid-19-booster-for-fall-booster-season-2022-03-10?mod=home-page (MarketWatch)] [https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/moderna-starts-study-of-hybrid-vaccine-that-targets-omicron-1.1735608 (BNN Bloomberg)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
**[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian Foreign Minister]] [[Sergey Lavrov]] and [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Ukraine)|Ukrainian Foreign Minister]] [[Dmytro Kuleba]] hold talks in [[Ankara]], [[Turkey]]. These are the highest level talks between the two nations since the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|invasion]]. No ceasefire is reached, but the possibility of a meeting with [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] and [[Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] was discussed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/top-russian-ukrainian-diplomats-meet-first-time-since-invasion-2022-03-10/ (Reuters)]
**[[Ministry of Defence (Ukraine)|Ukrainian Defense Minister]] [[Oleksii Reznikov]] says that [[Ukraine]] is willing to accept Russia’s surrender “with understanding”. [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/3425878-ukraine-to-accept-russias-surrender-with-understanding-defense-minister.html (Ukrinform)]
*[[Qatar–United States relations]], [[Colombia–United States relations]]
**U.S. President [[Joe Biden]] designates [[Qatar]] as a [[Major non-NATO ally]] and announces his intention to designate [[Colombia]] with the same status. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-700983 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] 
*[[Russia in the Council of Europe]]
**[[Russia]] announces that it will withdraw from the [[Council of Europe]]. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2022/03/10/russia-quits-europes-rule-of-law-body-sparking-questions-over-death-penalty-a76854 (''The Moscow Times'')] [https://tass.com/politics/1026225 (TASS)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Judiciary of Poland]], [[Polish constitutional crisis]]
**The [[Constitutional Tribunal (Poland)|Constitutional Tribunal]], the highest court in [[Poland]], declares that the [[European Court of Human Rights]] (ECHR) may not control the validity of the appointment of any judges in Poland. The Tribunal also wrote in its opinion that Poland is not obliged to implement four ECHR court rulings which found that the parties were denied a [[right to fair trial]], as the [[Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights|relevant provision]] violates the [[Constitution of Poland]] when applied to control the judges' appointment. [https://www.rp.pl/sady-i-trybunaly/art35839361-jest-wyrok-trybunalu-ws-wniosku-ziobry (''Rzeczpospolita'')] [https://www.euronews.com/2022/03/10/polish-court-finds-european-human-rights-convention-incompatible-with-constitution (Euronews)]
*The [[Israel]]i [[Knesset]] votes 45–15 to bar [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] spouses of [[Israelis]] from obtaining [[Israeli citizenship law|citizenship]] if they came from the [[West Bank]] or the [[Gaza Strip]], and blocks [[family reunification]] of Israelis and their spouses if they came from "enemy countries" such as [[Lebanon]], [[Syria]], and [[Iran]]. This replaces a similar emergency order that was in place from 2003 to last year, when it failed to receive enough votes to be annually renewed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israels-knesset-passes-law-barring-palestinian-spouses-2022-03-10/ (Reuters)]
*The [[National Electoral Board of Ethiopia]] condemns the arrest of the chairman of the [[Oromo Liberation Front]], [[Dawud Ibsa Ayana]], as illegal. The National Electoral Board also said it would investigate the reported arrest of opposition politicians from several other regions including [[Benishangul-Gumuz Region|Benishangul Gumuz]], [[Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples' Region|South Ethiopia]], [[South West Ethiopia]], [[Sidama Region|Sidama]], [[Oromia]], and [[Addis Ababa]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2022/03/10/ethiopia-opposition-figure-under-house-arrest-electoral-board-demands-his-release// (AfricaNews)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Hungarian presidential election]]
**[[Fidesz]]'s [[Katalin Novák]] is elected the first female [[president of Hungary]] by the [[National Assembly (Hungary)|National Assembly]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-10/hungary-elects-orban-loyalist-as-nation-s-first-female-president (Bloomberg)]
*[[2022 South Korean presidential election]]
**[[Conservatism|Conservative]] opposition leader [[Yoon Suk-yeol]] is confirmed as the winner of yesterday's [[Presidential elections in South Korea|presidential election]] with 48.59% of the vote. He will take office as [[President of South Korea]] on May 10. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-60685141 (BBC News)]
*[[2024 United States presidential election]]
**Former [[Montana]] [[Secretary of State of Montana|Secretary of State]] and [[Montana Senate|State Senator]] [[Corey Stapleton]] announces that he will form a "test the waters" [[political action committee]] in preparation to seek the nomination for the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] for the upcoming 2024 election. [https://www.greatfallstribune.com/story/news/politics/2022/03/12/former-montana-sos-stapleton-considering-2024-presidential-run/65344261007/ (''Great Falls Tribune'')]
 
'''Sports'''
*[[Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
***The [[Government of the United Kingdom|British government]] sanctions [[Russian oligarch]] and [[Chelsea F.C.]] owner [[Roman Abramovich]], freezing all his assets in the [[United Kingdom]]. The sanctions mean that [[Premier League]] club Chelsea will not be able to sell any more tickets for games, its merchandise store will be closed, and it will be unable to buy or sell players on the [[transfer market]] until the club is sold. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-60690362 (BBC News)]
*[[2022 Major League Baseball season]]
**[[2021–22 Major League Baseball lockout]]
***[[Major League Baseball]] reaches a labor [[Collective agreement|collective bargaining agreement]] with the [[Major League Baseball Players Association]] to end the lockout and salvage a 162-game season. Opening day will begin on April 7 and training camp will begin tomorrow. [https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/33399466/mlb-mlbpa-reach-labor-agreement-everything-need-know-lockout-ends (ESPN)]
